entries.sense_en: suggesting that something bad is about to happen
entries.sense_ko: 불길한, 나쁜 일이 일어날 것 같은

synonyms.nuance: Suggests direct danger or a warning aimed at someone; less about a vague feeling of doom.
Suggests hidden evil or wickedness, not just coming trouble.
Dark or sad in mood; does not predict that anything will happen.

entries.sense_en: a guess about something, based on too little evidence

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and informal; may have no evidence at all.
Often a longer, wider guessing, common in news and gossip.
A formal idea to be tested, mainly in science.

entries.sense_en: the punishment of being forced to leave a place

synonyms.nuance: Often long-term, and can also mean the state of living away from home.
synonyms.example: He lived in exile for ten years.

synonyms.nuance: Official removal of a foreigner from a country.
Forced removal from a group or school, not necessarily from a place far away.

entries.sense_en: a large branch of a tree

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary word for any limb of a tree, large or small.
synonyms.example: a branch of the oak tree

synonyms.nuance: A large main branch; also used for arms and legs.
A very small, thin branch, much smaller than a bough.

entries.sense_en: in reality; actually (used to add a true detail)

synonyms.nuance: Shorter and more common in everyday speech.
Casual; often corrects a wrong idea.
Spoken and a little formal; introduces a surprising or added detail.
synonyms.example: As a matter of fact, I know him.

entries.sense_en: a deep, narrow valley with steep sides

synonyms.nuance: A deep narrow valley worn by running water; the general word.
Smaller and shallower than a gulch, cut by rain water.
Bigger and rockier; a huge gorge, often with a river.

entries.sense_en: to pay back money that someone has lost or spent
entries.sense_ko: (쓴 돈이나 잃은 돈을) 갚아 주다, 변제하다

synonyms.nuance: General: give back money you owe or borrowed.
A shop or company returns money for a purchase.
Pay for a loss or harm, not only for money spent.

entries.sense_en: sent away by force from a place

synonyms.nuance: Force out of a group, school or country; broader than deport.
Send away as a punishment, often for political reasons.
Literary; order someone to leave a place forever.

entries.sense_en: a group of people riding horses or vehicles in a line

synonyms.nuance: Any orderly line of people moving forward, often at a ceremony.
A public show with marching or floats.
Vehicles or ships travelling together for safety.

entries.sense_en: swear words shouted out in anger

synonyms.nuance: A rude or angry word; can also mean a spell that brings bad luck.
The plain everyday term for a rude word.
Old-fashioned for a swear word; also a solemn promise.

entries.sense_en: a strong curse aimed at someone or something

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; a wish that harm will come.
Formal and literary word for a spoken curse.
Public, strong criticism; not a wish for harm.

entries.sense_en: a wish to harm others; a hateful look or feeling

synonyms.nuance: Common; the wish to hurt someone, often in words or acts.
Open unfriendliness or opposition.
Petty wish to annoy or hurt, often out of envy.
synonyms.example: She did it out of spite.

entries.sense_en: dirty and wet from trailing through mud; untidy

synonyms.nuance: The usual modern form; messy, wet and dirty.
Untidy hair or clothes, not necessarily wet or muddy.
Just dirty; no idea of being wet or limp.

entries.sense_en: playful flirting to attract attention

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; playful romantic behavior, can be brief.
The plain, common word for the action.
Literary; a light, unserious romance or play.

entries.sense_en: very steep, like the edge of a cliff

synonyms.nuance: The common word; can be gentle or very sharp.
Almost straight up and down, like a wall.
Sudden change of slope or manner; less about danger of falling.

entries.sense_en: knowing what will happen before it happens

synonyms.nuance: Wise planning for the future; ordinary skill, not magical knowing.
synonyms.example: He had the foresight to save.

synonyms.nuance: Knowing a fact in advance, often without a clear cause.
A vague feeling, usually of danger, before it happens.

entries.sense_en: spoken protests trying to stop someone from doing something

synonyms.nuance: Common; any objection, public or private.
A simple statement of disagreement, less urgent.
Blames someone for what they have done; remonstrance tries to stop them.

entries.sense_en: eager to fight or quarrel

synonyms.nuance: Common; ready to attack, in action as well as attitude.
Almost the same; sounds hostile and quarrelsome in a current situation.
Likes to argue or compete, not necessarily fight physically.

entries.sense_en: a dazed, almost unconscious state, here caused by drink

synonyms.nuance: Confused shock, usually short; you are still awake.
synonyms.example: He walked around in a daze.

synonyms.nuance: A dreamlike state, as if hypnotized.
Literary; long dull inactivity of body and mind.

entries.sense_en: weepy and sentimental, as when drunk

synonyms.nuance: Neutral or slightly negative; full of tender feeling.
Sentimental in a sickly, exaggerated way.
Simply crying or close to it; does not suggest silliness.

entries.tip_ko: 막달라 마리아(Magdalene)의 옛 영어 이름 'Maudlin'에서 온 말로, 울며 참회하는 그녀의 모습에서 '눈물이 헤픈'이라는 뜻이 생겼습니다.

entries.sense_en: to give up before the contest is really finished

synonyms.nuance: The everyday phrase; stop trying.
An idiom from boxing; admit defeat.
Stop doing something, by choice; less about defeat.

entries.tip_ko: 포커에서 '카드를 던지고 판을 포기한다'는 데서 나온 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: lying down

synonyms.nuance: Leaning back or lying partly, often to rest.
Lying face down; also "likely to".
Lying face up on the back.

entries.sense_en: a person rejected and despised by society

synonyms.nuance: Common; someone driven out of a group or society.
Just not part of the group; not despised.
Someone forced to live away from their home country.

entries.sense_en: calm and even temper, especially in difficulty

synonyms.nuance: Calm control of yourself in a tense moment.
Plain word; a quiet state, not always under pressure.
Peaceful and untroubled, often lasting.

entries.sense_en: honest and innocent, with no tricks

synonyms.nuance: Lacks experience, so easily fooled; can be mildly critical.
Natural and simple, without pretending.
Free from guilt or evil; broader than guileless.

entries.sense_en: pleasant to look at; attractive in a healthy, simple way

synonyms.nuance: Common; pleasing, usually of girls and women.
General word for someone who draws interest, any age or sex.
Usually of men; may also mean strong and well-formed.

entries.sense_en: to take care of oneself without help

synonyms.nuance: The modern form of the idiom; the same meaning.
synonyms.example: The kids had to fend for themselves.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; may mean staying safe, not surviving alone.
Plain and spoken; emphasizes coping without help.
synonyms.example: She can manage on her own.

entries.sense_en: to talk at length, as if giving a speech

synonyms.nuance: Talk more loudly or say what you think; no idea of long speech.
Talk in a teaching or scolding way.
Casual; talk too long, often boring.

entries.sense_en: tied with a rope so an animal cannot wander

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for fastening anything.
synonyms.example: tie the horse to a post

synonyms.nuance: Fasten a horse or cart to something, often quickly.
synonyms.example: hitch the horse to the wagon

synonyms.nuance: Tie an animal's legs together to limit its movement.

entries.sense_en: of the woods; set in a peaceful forest scene

synonyms.nuance: Plain description: covered with trees.
Everyday word about forest areas.
Simple country life, not specifically trees.

entries.sense_en: made stiff and unable to feel, from cold

synonyms.nuance: Everyday adjective; no feeling in a body part.
Very cold, or unable to move; stronger and less exact.
Hard to move; not necessarily without feeling.

entries.sense_en: trapped in a place by heavy snow

synonyms.nuance: Formal or written; stuck because of snow.
Left without a way to leave, for any reason.
Separated from others, by snow, flood, or other causes.

entries.sense_en: criminal, like a thief's

synonyms.nuance: General for anything against the law.
Specifically stealing; plain and direct, not legal language.
Against the law, even minor; less serious than felonious.

entries.sense_en: in a low, quiet voice so that others cannot hear

synonyms.nuance: The everyday way; uses breath, not voice.
synonyms.example: She said it in a whisper.

synonyms.nuance: Muttering, often a complaint you don't want heard.
General; just not loud.

entries.sense_en: hidden and mysterious; not easy to explain

synonyms.nuance: Just not visible or known.
Strange and unexplained; not necessarily secret.
Deliberately kept from others.

entries.tip_ko: 요즘은 '오컬트(초자연적인 것)'라는 뜻으로 더 많이 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: caused the animals to run away in a wild rush

synonyms.nuance: Frighten away; no idea of a crowd rushing together.
Informal; startle an animal or person suddenly.
Move fast; neutral, no fear needed.

entries.sense_en: made quickly from what was at hand, without planning

synonyms.nuance: The common word; make or do something without preparation.
Informal; mostly for speaking or performing.
Informal; build something rough and quick.

entries.sense_en: a roof covering made of straw or branches

synonyms.nuance: Any roof material; the general word.
The plant material only, not the finished roof.
Anything laid over something; no special material.

entries.sense_en: hid away in a safe place for later

synonyms.nuance: Informal; hide money or things in a secret spot.
General; keep out of sight, not always for later.
Keep for future use, not necessarily secretly.

entries.sense_en: made pass pleasantly so it did not feel long

synonyms.nuance: Plain; spend time in a certain way.
Pass time pleasantly and idly; the closest modern phrase.
Win someone by attractive manner; can also fool.

entries.sense_en: in a way meant to be noticed and admired

synonyms.nuance: Bright or fancy in a way that gets attention.
Bold, colorful and lively; sometimes positive.
Talking proudly of what you have or can do.

entries.sense_en: loud, forceful use of the voice

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; loud speech of any kind.
A loud noise from many people, often demanding something.
Noisy confusion and anger among a crowd.
synonyms.example: The crowd was in an uproar.

entries.sense_en: in a short, wise-sounding way, as if giving a rule of life

synonyms.nuance: Short and full of meaning; positive.
Self-important; sounds proud and silly.
Brief and clear; no idea of preaching.

entries.sense_en: a period when good things keep happening

synonyms.nuance: Repeated wins in a game or sport.
Close in meaning; a period of luck that can be good or bad.
One single chance event, not a long series.

entries.sense_en: sympathy and sorrow for another's suffering

synonyms.nuance: General feeling of care for someone in trouble.
Can sound superior; feeling sorry from above.
Deep caring that wants to help.

entries.sense_en: a curse spoken against someone

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary word; spoken or magical.
Formal; a curse calling down evil.
Rude words meant to hurt; not a wish for bad luck.

entries.sense_en: full of bitter, abusive words

synonyms.nuance: Common; insulting and cruel, in words or acts.
Very sharp criticism, not necessarily rude words.
Full of hatred, like poison.

entries.sense_en: a grand, noble quality that fills you with awe

synonyms.nuance: Impressive size and splendor.
Royal dignity and beauty.
Moral greatness; not about scenery.

entries.sense_en: to be no longer a little child; not as young as others treat you

synonyms.nuance: Modern form, but now said of people well past youth.
Plain statement that someone is grown up.

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for someone no longer a child.

entries.sense_en: a strong, safe place that is hard to reach

synonyms.nuance: A place strongly defended, also for a group's base.
A big building for defense.
A place of safety, not necessarily defended.

entries.sense_en: clever at getting what you want by tricks

synonyms.nuance: Clever in a sly, often dishonest way.
Skilled at tricky plans; a bit playful.
Secretive and tricky, or teasing.

entries.sense_en: in a weak, complaining way

synonyms.nuance: Irritable over small things.
Worried and unhappy.
Childish bad temper when you can't have your way.

entries.sense_en: unhealthily pale

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; light skin or color.
Gray-white, from shock or fear.
Yellowish and sickly.

entries.sense_en: painful, hard effort and suffering

synonyms.nuance: Long, tiring hard work.
Suffering from lack of money or comfort.
Effort against difficulty; may be brief.

entries.sense_en: a covering, here a blanket of snow

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; a soft cover, or a thick layer.
A loose outer coat; also something that hides.
General; anything laid over something.

entries.sense_en: pale and tired-looking, as from illness or grief

synonyms.nuance: Just light in color.
Worn out and thin from worry or lack of sleep.
Face looks tight and tired from pain or worry.

entries.sense_en: to die (slang from poker: turning in your chips)
entries.sense_ko: 죽다 (포커에서 칩을 반납한다는 데서 나온 속어)

synonyms.nuance: Polite and gentle way to say die.
Slangy and jokey; not for serious talk.
Also from gambling; slang for dying.
